concept.title: Scenario 10 — Image Placed Inside a Positioned <div> (Text Box Equivalent)

conbody.p: Consider a document where the author has placed an image inside a <div> that is removed from the normal document flow using CSS (for example, position: absolute or position: fixed) to control its placement on the page, similar to a floating text box.

Result: The converter ignores the CSS positioning and any surrounding
content that isn't structurally part of the body flow, but it retains the element placed inside the positioned
. The extracted image is mapped to a DITA element, typically wrapped in a if it appears as a block image.
conbody.note: Do not place images inside CSS-positioned <div> containers that sit outside the normal document flow. Although the image may be retained, any surrounding positioned content can be lost during conversion.
